questions.stem: How is Coupling described in relation to software and systems?
options: A way of compressing data before it moves between systems
A technique for merging two databases into one
A parameter dependency approach used across software or across systems
A method of encrypting data in transit
A schema design pattern for a single application
questions.explanation: Coupling is a parameter dependency approach used when more than one software or system is involved in delivering a result.

options: Using data elements to kick off the next step in a different system
Storing the same data in two systems for redundancy
Joining two tables on a shared key
Copying a whole database to a backup location
Converting data from one format to another
questions.explanation: Data Coupling is when data elements are used to kick off the next step in a different system, creating a cross-system data dependency.

questions.stem: Which example is used to illustrate Data Coupling in a data pipeline?
options: A retailer reconciling daily sales totals at midnight
A bank archiving transactions older than seven years
A weather service publishing hourly forecasts
A social media feed being scanned for product mentions
A hospital management system in which a baby's data is pulled the moment the baby is registered
questions.explanation: The example given is pulling data from a hospital management system as soon as a newborn baby is registered in that system.

questions.stem: What is the disadvantage of the Data Coupling approach?
options: It requires all systems to share the same database
If something goes wrong in the first system, the dependent systems cannot move
It doubles the storage needed for every dataset
It only works with structured data
It prevents systems from being updated independently
questions.explanation: Because dependent systems wait on data from the first system, a failure in the first system stops the dependent systems from proceeding.

questions.stem: In the old file-loading example of Data Coupling, what was the core challenge when pulling files from another system?
options: Files were too large to fit on a single server
The file format changed with every load
The receiving system had no permission to read the files
Knowing when the file had been completely copied so that pulling could safely start
The source system deleted files as soon as they were written
questions.explanation: The pulling job had to wait until the whole file movement was complete, and the challenge was how to know when the copy had finished.

questions.stem: Which workaround for the file-copy challenge in Data Coupling involves renaming?
options: Copy the file under a different name, then rename it once the copy is complete so the pulling job can recognise it
Rename the source system so the pulling job cannot connect too early
Rename the pulling job after each successful run
Rename the target folder after the file has been read
Rename the file to include a timestamp before copying begins
questions.explanation: One workaround was to copy the file under a different name and, once fully copied, rename it so the pulling job could pick up the required file.

questions.stem: Which workaround for the file-copy challenge in Data Coupling relies on a temp file?
options: Write the data into a temp file and delete it once the pulling job has finished
Split the data file into several temp files that are pulled one by one
Create a temp file after the data file is completely copied, so the pulling job starts when it sees the temp file
Keep a temp file open for the whole duration of the copy
Store the file's checksum in a temp file before copying starts
questions.explanation: A temp file was created after the data file was completely copied; when the pulling job saw the temp file, it knew it could start pulling the data files.

questions.stem: How do modern export, copy or move commands signal that a file copy is still in progress?
options: They lock the destination folder until the copy finishes
They send an email notification on completion
They write a log entry that the pulling job must read
They keep the file hidden until it has been verified
They add tmp to the file name while in progress and remove it once the copy is done
questions.explanation: Modern commands include tmp in the file's naming convention while the copy is in progress and remove it when complete, so the pulling job can recognise the finished data file.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT among the listed types of coupling?
options: Stamp Coupling
Temporal Coupling
Control Coupling
External Coupling
Content Coupling
questions.explanation: The listed types are No Direct Coupling, Data Coupling, Stamp Coupling, Control Coupling, External Coupling, Comment Coupling and Content Coupling; Temporal Coupling is not among them.

questions.stem: Which of these is one of the listed types of coupling?
options: Schema Coupling
Network Coupling
Index Coupling
No Direct Coupling
Transaction Coupling
questions.explanation: No Direct Coupling is one of the listed types, alongside Data, Stamp, Control, External, Comment and Content Coupling.
